reason: The E4 comparison requires matched training runs on the GPU machine. The CPU analysis agent does not own the GPU and the frozen corpus is not local. This file freezes the protocol and definitions so the intervention can be executed without re-deriving them.

model_of_phenomenon.statement: A broad global hierarchy exists, but the exact high-mass population required for faithful computation is strongly context-dependent.
model_of_phenomenon.consequence: The stable core is descriptive population structure and a useful prior; it is NOT yet evidence that forcing the core to remain always-on is the optimal compute allocation.
model_of_phenomenon.evidence: results/arm_a_science/e4_forward_ablation.json: at matched 320 coords/head the ORACLE_DYNAMIC selection preserves the dense output far better than HYBRID or STATIC (4.0% vs 24.2% vs 83.3% relative logit perturbation); zero-u = 55.9%.

prediction.predeclared_ordering: DENSE > ORACLE_DYNAMIC > LEARNED_DYNAMIC > HYBRID > STATIC on fidelity/loss at matched active width, and LEARNED_DYNAMIC > HYBRID > STATIC on training loss at matched active compute.
prediction.rationale: STATIC misses the rotating u mass (global top-320 keeps 51.1% per token vs 98.9% for dynamic); HYBRID's fixed core consumes width that the tail could spend on per-context mass; ORACLE_DYNAMIC is the upper bound.
prediction.must_not_change: The ordering above must not be modified after seeing learned-router results. If LEARNED_DYNAMIC fails to beat HYBRID/STATIC, that is the result.
prediction.falsification: Any of: STATIC >= LEARNED_DYNAMIC, HYBRID > LEARNED_DYNAMIC at adaptive-router recall above the predeclared gate, or LEARNED_DYNAMIC not beating DENSE at matched width.

arms.DENSE: unmodified Arm-A at the same token budget (upper-bound control)
arms.STATIC: frozen global top-w u coordinates from the census, input-independent
arms.ORACLE_DYNAMIC: top-w from the true u activations (reference upper bound, not implementable)
arms.LEARNED_DYNAMIC: top-w selected by a learned router from the level input v; trained end-to-end
arms.HYBRID: always-on frozen core + learned router over the remaining K-c tail; core fractions from the predeclared ladder
additional_controls: routing shuffle: permuted router assignments with identical load
position-stratified control: route selection computed independently per position bin
expert knockout: drop the most-selected tail coordinate and measure loss change
width-matched random selection: random w coordinates per token at the same width

width_assignment.HYBRID: core c + tail t = w, with c in {128 (3.125%), 256 (6.25%)} and t = w - c

matched_width_design.freeze_rule: Core membership and the global ranking are frozen from the E3 census before training; core fraction must not be tuned per task or per example.

router_bridge.question: Can a learned router recover enough of the oracle dynamic selection to retain its fidelity advantage?
router_bridge.input: v at each level (D=256) after layer norm; per head or pooled over heads (D -> H*K or D -> K)

required_metrics.oracle_topk_recall: fraction of the oracle top-w u coordinates recovered
required_metrics.oracle_mass_recall: fraction of oracle top-w u mass recovered (primary router metric)
required_metrics.logit_distortion: relative L2 logit perturbation vs dense
required_metrics.loss: training/validation loss at matched active width and at matched wall-clock
required_metrics.tokens_to_threshold: tokens to reach the dense control's loss at a fixed step budget
required_metrics.coordinate_utilization: fraction of coordinates selected at least once
required_metrics.systems_throughput: tokens/s and update ms measured same-session against the dense control

router_bridge.predeclared_gate: a trained router below 0.5 oracle-mass-recall@64 at matched width must be reported as a negative result for the learned dynamic/hybrid arms
router_bridge.analysis: plot fidelity (logit distortion, loss) against oracle-mass recall for each router checkpoint; the learned dynamic arm is only competitive if it stays near the oracle frontier

mechanism: repeated motifs (the E2 recurrence probe predicts content-driven persistence; test under training)
tasks.language: frozen-corpus held-out windows using the E3 sampling frame, or an explicit fixed held-out split

metrics: loss AUC and tokens-to-threshold at matched active coordinates/token
relative logit distortion before/after each intervention
wall-clock per update and tokens/s, same-session against the dense Arm-A control
router entropy, coordinate utilization, load-balance coefficient of variation
kernel/runtime cost of the routed path

behavioral_checks.expert_knockout: zero the top-1 most selected tail coordinate and report loss delta; a functional specialist should show a measurable delta
behavioral_checks.routing_shuffle: permute router assignments within a batch preserving load; loss must degrade if routing is functional
behavioral_checks.position_control: recompute routing per position bin; if the advantage vanishes, it is positional

statistics.unit_of_resampling: document/block bootstrap; tokens are not independent replicates
statistics.seeds: at least 2 training seeds per arm; one trajectory is not replication
statistics.report: effect sizes with confidence intervals; primary metric is loss at matched active width

decision_rule.architecture_informing: any arm that beats the dense control at matched wall-clock, or beats STATIC at matched active width, changes the recommended architecture
decision_rule.paper_central: LEARNED_DYNAMIC > STATIC and LEARNED_DYNAMIC >= HYBRID at matched active width, reproduced across seeds and both task families, with a systems path preserving the wall-clock advantage
decision_rule.stop_rule: If learned routing cannot beat static on loss at matched width, the correct conclusion is that the measured conditionality does not translate into a practical routing win; report it and stop.

pilot_evidence.status: E4-pilot / oracle intervention; not E4 evidence
pilot_evidence.summary: At 320 coords/head: oracle-dynamic 4.0% relative logit perturbation, hybrid 24.2%, static 83.3%, zero-u 55.9% (all cross-fitted, matched width, 8 held-out windows).
pilot_evidence.falsified: The previous HYBRID-first fidelity prediction (hybrid < dynamic < static) is falsified and must not be softened.

dependencies.e3: results/arm_a_science/e3_contract.json + campaigns/E3_G4_SCIENCE_CELL.md freeze the census sampling and core/ranking definitions
dependencies.systems: G4 systems validation of the routed path (from the parallel optimization track) supplies the wall-clock measurement

execution_notes: Freeze the core ranking and width before training; never recompute per checkpoint or example.
Report the census numbers next to the intervention so the population-to-architecture chain stays auditable.
If HYBRID wins despite lower fidelity, report the systems reason explicitly rather than relabeling the hypothesis.
